root_idea.summary: The root has a central orientation of breaking apart or cutting off.
root_idea.development: From this orientation develop verbs for cutting, breaking, and severing; nouns for fragments and separated portions; and specialized terms for broken grain, gold-bearing stones, and severed bodily or relational states.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested noun denoting resulting fragments or pieces.
Distinct Quran-attested passive participle with the construction of an uninterrupted or uncut-short gift.

senses.usage_conditions: In 21:58, it describes the idols after they have been broken into pieces; the noun denotes the resulting fragments rather than the act of breaking.
In 11:108, it occurs in the negative expression عَطَاءٌ غَيْرُ مَجْذُوذٍ, describing a gift or stipend that is not cut short or interrupted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut or cut off a thing, especially utterly or quickly; to cut the fruit from palm trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cutting may be intensive, repeated, or extensive. In a figurative battle expression, cutting people off utterly means exterminating them by slaughter.
The object may be a thing generally, including a hard thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten something or to hasten to it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an additional Form I use attested in a proverb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become cut or cut off, utterly or quickly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VII has an intransitive or passive-like construction and may describe something becoming severed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece broken off; a fragment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is used for pieces or fragments.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece of rag or clothing; anything serving as a garment or covering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may refer to any piece of clothing used to cover the body.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of separating one thing from another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An alternative transmitted gloss as “superiority” is reported in the evidence as probably a mistranscription.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Small pieces or particles of silver; silver cuttings or clippings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized noun for silver in broken or cut pieces.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Stones containing gold or other valuable material.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation is explained by the stones being broken or crushed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Distinct parties, portions, or divisions of people or things.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a collective or plural-like use for separated portions.
The description may include being cut off utterly or quickly, as well as being broken.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A preparation of parched barley or wheat broken into coarse particles and made into a drinkable food; also a portion of such food consumed at one time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is connected with the grain being broken into coarse particles.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Amputated, specifically of an arm or hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It is also used figuratively in this sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Severed or not closely maintained, of a bond of relationship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression describes a relationship not joined or sustained by affection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Much broken or broken into pieces, of a tooth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an anatomical descriptive use.
An alternate vocalization is also transmitted for the same lexical item.
